note: Adapted from the species description by Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldier, hence no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and several rows of the worker measurement table misaligned by OCR are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparison with A. chirotus is given in the discussion of that species. Body size about the same as in A. tithasus, but the postclypeus is much more inflated in both the alate and the worker, and the ocelli are closer to the compound eye. This is the only species of the genus in which the worker has overlapping midgut and hindgut and a slender fore tibia with a reduced third apical spur. In the alate this character is somewhat doubtful: the third apical spur is reduced in the type series, whereas another pair of alates apparently conspecific has it fully developed. The alate of A. imbellis is distinguished by its very small fontanelle, longer mandibular apical teeth and broader meso- and metanotum. The worker abdomen of this species possibly dehisces, but this is not certain.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity pale yellow, setae sparse. Postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.33–0.35. Mandibular apical teeth long, La/Li 0.81–0.82, Ra/Rn 0.97–1.00; left accessory marginal tooth distant from the molar prominence and separated from it by a distinct notch in surface view, La/Li·Lm 20.75–21.20; anterior margins of first and second marginal teeth subequal, Ra/Ri·Rm 22.80. Fore tibia hardly thickened, Ti/Tw 5.25–5.30, third spur reduced, one quarter the length of the other two spurs or less. Overlap of midgut and hindgut about twice the width of the midgut at the insertion of the Malpighian tubules, the anterior end of the hindgut touching the Malpighian node; valve seat dorsolateral in the undissected abdomen; internal cushions of the valve about equally and rather distinctly developed, surface scaly, posterior margin of each scale with a small point or spine. Valve membrane outside the cushions with numerous minute spines tending to be arranged in rows. Other characters as in the genus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark sepia brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle small, about half the size of an ocellus, slightly concave, short oval, brown; middle spot slightly smaller, flat, on a slightly raised short oval area, sepia brown; postclypeus sepia brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal band sepia brown, somewhat indistinct, flat crescent-shaped; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum sepia brown, transverse dark sutures distinct; femora yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites sepia brown, dorsal spiracles darker; sternites brown laterally, pale yellowish brown medially, ventral spiracles sepia brown; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule slightly wavy, not quite evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by slightly less than half to two thirds their minimum diameter; postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.31–0.33, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture strongly developed. Mandibular apical teeth rather long, La/Lj 0.68–0.76, Ra/Ri 0.92–0.99; left accessory marginal tooth just free of the molar prominence in surface view, La/Li·Lm 11.59–12.18; tip of first marginal tooth of right mandible only very slightly behind the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, anterior margin of first marginal tooth distinctly longer than that of second. Head capsule pilosity sepia brown, coarse, uneven, not forming a coat. Meso- and metanotum rather narrow at the constriction, M/W 0.25–0.28. Third apical spur of fore tibia reduced, one fifth the length of the other two spurs or less; this is so in the type series, whereas specimens from another nest have it fully developed.
